generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A structured control can advertise a current subject while the referenced raw evidence still identifies an older subject, creating a metadata-to-evidence provenance split.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Rewrite only structured head fields and preserve stale raw evidence bytes or accept evidence without content-address verification.
trigger_signals: structured evidence carries a subject identifier
raw evidence contains its own current-subject marker
evidence is transported in a result-only package
an older subject remains mentioned in raw evidence

reusable_control.procedure: Compare the expected subject with current-subject markers in raw evidence and verify the content hash before accepting the evidence.

generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Every control that cites raw evidence must declare where the bytes are resolved, bind them to the intended material subject and content hash, and avoid ambiguous ancestor-as-current wording.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Reject a control when its raw evidence current-subject marker differs from the expected subject or when the referenced bytes do not match the certified content hash.

transfer_cases.evidence: A synthetic raw evidence fixture presenting an ancestor as current is rejected by the generic subject checker.
A current-subject evidence file with a deliberately incorrect expected content hash is rejected.

skill_changes.change: Applied explicit evidence-location, evidence-subject and content-address bindings to critical controls before publication.
Added a transferable subject/content checker and discriminant stale-subject plus hash-mismatch siblings to the delivery evidence package.
